questions.q: Which is NOT an assumption of perfect competition?
questions.why: Perfect competition assumes a very large number of small producers.

questions.q: For a perfectly competitive firm, which is true?
questions.why: Every extra unit sells at the same market price.

questions.q: A perfectly competitive firm makes {q} units. The market price is £{p} and its ATC is £{a}. What is its profit, in £?
Firms in a perfectly competitive market are making abnormal profit. What happens in the long run?
options: Firms enter, supply rises and price falls
Firms leave, supply falls and price rises
questions.why: Free entry shifts market supply right until only normal profit is left.

questions.q: In long-run equilibrium, a perfectly competitive firm is both productively and allocatively efficient.
questions.why: P = MC at the lowest point of ATC.

questions.q: Which is a valid criticism of the claim that perfect competition gives the best outcome?
options: Normal profits leave little to spend on research
questions.why: With only normal profit and perfect knowledge, firms have little means or reason to innovate.

questions.q: Explain why a firm in perfect competition is a price taker.

ideas.label: There are very many firms, so one firm can't affect the market price
Products are identical and knowledge is perfect, so a higher price loses all customers

questions.model: There are so many firms that one firm cannot affect the market price. Products are identical and buyers have perfect knowledge, so charging more would lose all its customers.
questions.why: One firm is too small to matter, and buyers can switch at no cost.

tests.answer: There are many firms so one firm can't affect the price. Products are identical, so a higher price would lose all its customers.
